answer: Each applicant tends one trellis in a tundra greenhouse, a vine from seed stock keyed to its public key. Eight pruning rounds follow: each cut's pattern comes from the last cut plus the seed stock, and the holder files the sap reading before the next round opens. A copied filing fails: no two vines share a growth pattern, and a stale cut never matches fresh sap. At the eighth round the vine yields a single pearl whose skin carries the vine's cut history. One trellis costs $260 plus 40 greenhouse days; 5,000 fakes need 5,000 trellises, $1.3 million and 200,000 days; one bay grows one vine.
